newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Siemens wins 72.5mln DM Nigeria contracts.
newsitem.headline: Siemens wins 72.5mln DM Nigeria contracts.

text.p: Germany's Siemens has signed two deals worth 72.5 million marks with state-run Nigerian Telecommunications (NITEL) to provide 60,000 telephone lines, a NITEL spokesman said on Friday.
"The deals were signed at the end of September for the restoration of exchanges destroyed by fire at Ikeja and Apapa and to provide new lines in Port Harcourt," the spokesman said.
The project to restore the burnt Ikeja exchange, providing 30,000 lines, and to provide another 10,000 lines in south eastern Port Harcourt is to be completed within eight months.
The other project, for 20,000 lines in Apapa has a completion period of 10 months.
The amounts of 192.5 million naira and 132.3 million naira respectively will also be paid for the two projects.
Siemens officials in Lagos were unavailable for comment.
Some of Nigeria's biggest businesses had communications severed by separate fires at the exchange in the Apapa district of Lagos in 1996, and at the Ikeja district in July.
Nigeria's military government has said that NITEL is a target for privatisation, although no date has yet been set.
